answer: One concrete sybil brake is a bonded admission ticket: each new identity must lock a non-refundable compute relic—a short proof-of-work tied to the epoch seed—before it can vote or claim emission. When a gale of clone keys arrives, the attacker cost grows linearly per identity, so flooding seats becomes uneconomic. Peers then grade a sonnet-length mechanism essay for originality; ledger-level duplicate rejection drops farms that recycle the same text.
